mentions.name: Chess67
mentions.description: A platform for running over-the-board chess: coaches can sell lessons and manage scheduling and payments, clubs can run events and communicate with players, and tournaments can handle registrations, with pairing and USCF submission in progress.
mentions.problem: Running over-the-board chess events is fragmented: registrations happen in Google Forms, payments via Venmo/Zelle, pairings in SwissSys/WinTD, and communication across email and text. The main challenge is matching existing workflows, especially Swiss pairings, which are more nuanced than they look.
mentions.audience: Chess clubs, coaches, and tournament organizers.
mentions.source_excerpt: I’m working on https://chess67.com, software for running over-the-board chess (clubs, coaches, tournaments).

mentions.name: Chess67
mentions.description: Chess67 is a platform for chess coaches, clubs, and tournament organizers to manage their operations in one place, handling registrations, payments, scheduling, rosters, lessons, memberships, and tournament files (TRF/DBF) while cutting out the usual mix of spreadsheets and scattered tools.
mentions.problem: Solves the practical workflow problems chess coaches deal with every day and makes it easier for local chess communities to run events smoothly, replacing spreadsheets and scattered tools.
mentions.audience: Chess coaches, club organizers, and tournament directors
